column4: Visit note | 2025-04-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Tasnim Kabir, 52, female. Ms. Kabir explains that she suffers from a throbbing headache on one side and needs to lie down in a dark room when it strikes. She works as a garment factory worker and mentions that her symptoms are worse since starting night shifts at a hospital in Rangpur. She denies any visual loss, numbness, or weakness in her limbs. On examination: about 7 headache days a month, BP 119/83 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 54 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and neurological findings are unremarkable. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
